audit_level.description: Audit logging level: 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled (logs security-relevant events)

auth_mechanisms.description: Authentication mechanisms the broker supports; values like 'EXTERNAL', 'DBUS_COOKIE_SHA1', 'ANONYMOUS'

inactivity_timeout.description: Timeout (in seconds) before closing inactive connections. Note: dbus-broker does NOT support inactivity_timeout in config XML; this directive is not documented. Removed from template and schema.

introspection_enabled.description: Whether to allow introspection via org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable. Disable for production security hardening.

listen_addresses.description: List of transport addresses the broker listens on

listen_backlog.description: Maximum number of pending connections in the kernel listen queue

log_level.description: Log verbosity level; acceptable values are 'error', 'warning', 'info', 'debug' — but the broker itself does not expose this in config XML; it's controlled via --log=fd and not configurable via XML. Removed from template and schema.

max_bytes_per_user.description: Maximum number of bytes of message payload each user may allocate. From CLI option --max-bytes=16MiB.

max_fds.description: Maximum number of file descriptors the broker may open system-wide per user (NOT total for broker process). The CLI option --max-fds sets per-user limit, default 64.

max_fds_per_connection.description: Maximum number of file descriptors that may be passed per connection

max_matches_per_user.description: Maximum number of match rules each user may allocate. From CLI option --max-matches=16k.

max_message_size.description: Maximum size (in bytes) of a single message (e.g., 100 MB)

max_objects_per_user.description: Maximum total number of names, peers, pending replies, etc each user may allocate. From CLI option --max-objects=16k.

max_outstanding_messages.description: Maximum number of queued messages per connection

service_activation.description: Service to auto-start on bus initialization (e.g., system-wide service). Optional.

user_rules.description: Per-user connection limits and privileges. At least one user rule should be present.
